title: Consent authority record: likeness and digital replica profile (draft 0.2.0)
description: The JSON document a consent authority returns when a verifier resolves the `uri` of a CAWG `cawg.consent` reference whose `reference_type` is `consent_authority`. One record covers one consent relationship with one living adult participant: the signed agreement versions, the history of every later change, payment evidence and the C2PA assets registered under it. It never contains biometric data. Draft 0.2.0, 2026-10-27. Tracks the CAWG consent assertion 1.0 draft, content v0.21. Not affiliated with or endorsed by CAWG, DIF or C2PA. JSON Schema cannot express every rule: spec/README.md defines the signing statements, the state derivation and the validation rules a verifier also applies.

example.description: true marks illustrative data. A consumer MUST NOT treat a record with `example: true` as consent.

record_uri.description: The URI carried in the `uri` field of the `cawg.consent` references that point to this record. It never changes; it SHOULD be a persistent identifier that a successor authority can redirect.

agreements.description: Every signed version of the agreement, oldest first. Version n + 1 restates the whole agreement, names version n by digest, and replaces it from the time its `version_added` event takes effect.

salt.description: At least 16 random bytes, base64url without padding.

disclosures.description: Present only in the full view. Maps each commitment digest to the salt and value it commits to. Removing this member yields the public view; every signature and the authority attestation verify on both views.

authority_attestation.description: The serving authority's signature over this record without `disclosures` and without this member. Its `signed_at` equals `state.as_of`.

profileId.description: Identifies this profile and version. The `.example` host is a placeholder until a persistent identifier is registered.

httpsUri.description: An https URI whose authority is a host name, an IPv4 address or a bracketed IPv6 address, with an optional port: no userinfo (RFC 9110 §4.2.4) and no percent-encoding, so that every URI parser finds the same host (R10).

extensionUri.description: An absolute URI naming a value defined outside this profile.

localId.description: An identifier that is unique within this record.

actorId.description: A `party_id`, or the `id` of a consent authority.

dateTime.description: RFC 3339 date-time in UTC (`Z`), to the millisecond at most, without leap seconds. Validators assert `format`, which also rejects impossible dates such as 30 February. Values are compared as instants, so `09:58:00.5Z` and `09:58:00.500Z` are equal.

sha256Base64url.description: A SHA-256 digest, base64url without padding.

digest.description: Digest of the exact bytes of a document that is not embedded, for example a signed PDF or an invoice.

commitment.description: Stands in for a withheld value: base64url(SHA-256(UTF-8(JCS([salt, value])))). The salt and value appear in `disclosures` in the full view.

value.description: Decimal amount as a string, so no precision is lost.

percent.description: A percentage from 0 to 100 as a decimal string.

languageTag.description: A BCP 47 language tag limited to language, extended language, script, region and variant subtags.

identityAttribute.description: The attributes CAWG consent v0.21 names for identity consent.

anyOf.description: replica.create: build a digital replica (scan, avatar, voice model). replica.modify: change or retrain it. media.generate: make new media depicting the participant. media.alter: change existing recordings of the participant with AI. model.train: train or fine-tune any other AI model on the participant's attributes.
Entry keys of the CAWG training and data mining assertion 1.1.
Make derivative works of the asset.

authority.description: The authority serving this response. It is the authority in charge: version 1's `authority_id`, or the last authority that an `authority_transferred` event handed the record to.

contact.description: Where to send questions and withdrawals.

keys_uri.description: A JWK Set (RFC 7517) on the same origin as `id`, listing the keys that sign attestations and events, including the keys of earlier signatures.

continuity.description: How records stay resolvable if this authority stops or hands over (CAWG consent v0.21 §5, record continuity and succession).

successor_authority.description: An authority designated to take over the records.

escrow.description: How records are escrowed, in plain words.

signatures.description: One signature per signing party. The participant and every licensee of a grant sign each version. Any other party signs a version that changes its party entry, or adds, changes or drops a compensation item it pays or receives (or a grant that names that item), a grant it holds, its asset terms or `asset_rights` entries, or the biometric declaration naming it as holder (R6). A representative may also sign; it never signs in the participant's place.

agreement.description: The signed part of one version. Nothing in it ever changes. It names the profile, the record and the authority, so it cannot be presented under another record or authority.

authority_id.description: The authority that the parties instruct to hold this record. It is the authority in charge when the version is recorded.

previous_version_digest.description: `agreement_digest.value` of version n - 1. Absent in version 1.

language.description: Language of the human-readable texts in this agreement.

items.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or ISO 3166-2 code, for example `US-NY` or `DK`.

jurisdictions.description: Jurisdictions the parties considered when drafting. Informational; not a choice-of-law clause.

parties.description: Exactly one participant, and a licensee when the version has a grant. A work showing several people has one record, and one `cawg.consent` reference, per person.

terms.description: At least one term (CAWG consent v0.21 §5).

compensation.description: Every agreed payment. Grants reference these by `compensation_id`; an unpaid grant references an item with model `unpaid`.

end_of_use.description: Required when the version has a grant.

asset_rights.description: Licensing posture of the assets made under this agreement, declared by their rights holders.

retention.description: How long the authority keeps this record.

disclosures_until.description: When the authority deletes `disclosures`. Commitments and signatures stay verifiable afterwards.

record_until.description: When the authority deletes the record. null: kept while any registered asset may still be in circulation, under `authority.continuity`.

roles.description: `participant` is the natural person whose identity attributes the terms cover (CAWG consent v0.21). `authorized_representative` acts for the participant. `rights_holder` holds rights in the assets made under the agreement.

scheme.description: `human_consent_id` is optional and creates no dependency on any registry. `x509_sha256` is the base64url SHA-256 of a DER certificate the party signs with, for certificates that name it by neither a domain nor an LEI (for example a person's qualified certificate).

verification.description: For the participant: identity and adulthood were checked. No date of birth is recorded.

identity_binding.description: For the participant: values a verifier can match against the named actor of a `cawg.identity` assertion that a reference's `bound_actor` points to.

represents.description: For an authorized representative: the participant's `party_id`.

authorization_evidence.description: Digest of the document that authorizes the representative.

consentDocument.description: The human-readable written consent the participant read and signed for this version.

separate_document.description: Whether the consent is a document of its own rather than a clause of another agreement. New York asks a model management company to obtain it separately from the representation agreement (Labor Law §1034(11)).

territories.description: Either `["WORLD"]` with optional exclusions, or a list of countries.

to.description: The only parties a sublicense may go to. Absent: any party.

limited_to.description: What a sublicensee may do, in plain words.

max_assets.description: Upper limit on the number of assets registered under the term.

named_works.description: Campaigns, products or titles the term is limited to. Absent: not limited to named works.

term_id.description: Stable across versions. A term id that a version drops, or that is withdrawn or ended, never returns in a later version.

kind.description: A grant permits the listed uses within its scope. A prohibition forbids the listed uses to everyone, whatever any grant says.

consent_domain.description: Same values as `consent_domain` in `cawg.consent`. Identity terms are declared by the participant; asset terms by a rights holder named in `declared_by`.

declared_by.description: For asset terms: the declaring rights holder's `party_id`.

description.description: What the use is for, specific enough for the participant to recognise it.

licensees.description: The parties that may exercise the grant.

valid_until.description: Exclusive end. Required for grants. A prohibition without it has no end.

withdrawal_right.description: Whether the agreement lets the declaring party withdraw the grant before `valid_until` without breach. A recorded withdrawal takes effect in this record either way; this flag records the contractual position only.

compensation.description: `compensation_id` values that pay for the grant.

end_of_use.description: Overrides the agreement's `end_of_use` for this grant.

license_uri.description: The license that applies, when `posture` is `licensed`.

contact.description: Where to ask for a license.

amount.description: The rate of pay. For `per_asset` and `per_period` it is the amount per unit.

basis.description: The unit or base, for example `per published video` or `net revenue of the campaign`.

cap.description: Maximum total payable under this item, in the currency of `amount`.

action.description: What happens to assets already published.
`not_applicable`: the grant makes no replica, or no source captures.

retain_until.description: For `retain_without_use`: when the retained copy is deleted.

replica.description: The digital replica itself (avatar, voice model, trained weights).

source_captures.description: Photos, scans and recordings made to build the replica.

endOfUse.description: What happens when a grant reaches its `valid_until` or a version drops it (`on_expiry`), and when it is withdrawn or a narrowing ends it early (`on_withdrawal`). New uses stop in every case. There is no notice period in the record: a withdrawal takes effect when the authority receives it, or at a later instant the party signs.

withdrawal_channels.description: Ways the authority accepts a withdrawal. No particular form is required of the participant.

biometricIdentifiers.description: A declaration about biometric identifiers. It never contains them.

held_by_authority.description: The authority holds no biometric identifiers, templates or embeddings for this record.

restriction.description: The default restriction of CAWG consent v0.21 §5: biometric identifiers collected for this engagement are not used for any unrelated purpose.

collected_in_engagement.description: Whether a party derives biometric identifiers for this engagement, for example face geometry from a scan.

publicJwk.description: A public JWK (RFC 7517). Private key members are forbidden.

keyBinding.description: Why the key in `jwk` belongs to the signer, and who holds it.

method.description: did: `jwk` is a verification method in the signer's DID document. x509: `jwk` is the public key of the first certificate in `x5c`, which is tied to the signer by an identifier listed in clear: a `dNSName` subjectAltName equal to one of its `domain` identifiers, an LEI (ISO 17442-2) equal to one of its `lei` identifiers, or the certificate's SHA-256 equal to one of its `x509_sha256` identifiers. authority_verified: the authority checked the signer's identity and recorded the key.

did_url.description: A DID URL with a fragment. Its only `#` is the fragment delimiter (RFC 3986 §3.5).

x5c.description: Certificate chain, leaf first, standard base64 DER (RFC 7515 §4.1.6).

custody.description: signer_held: only the signer controls the private key. authority_managed: the authority holds the key and signs when the signer authenticates.

authentication.description: For authority_managed keys: how the signer authenticated before the authority signed.

verified_by.description: The authority in charge at `verified_at`: it verified the binding, or holds the key.

signature.description: A compact JWS (RFC 7515) with a detached, unencoded payload (RFC 7797). The payload is the RFC 8785 form of the signing statement that spec/README.md defines; a verifier rebuilds it from the record.

alg.description: Fully specified algorithms. `Ed25519` as registered by RFC 9864, `ML-DSA-65` by RFC 9964.

kid.description: RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of `jwk`, also the `kid` of the protected header.

value.description: `<protected header>..<signature>`. The header is exactly {alg, b64: false, crit: ["b64"], kid}.

timestamp_token.description: Optional RFC 3161 time-stamp token, standard base64 DER, over SHA-256 of the decoded JWS signature bytes. On an agreement or event signature it cannot be added later: once the version or event is recorded, the record's digests cover it.

state.description: The mutable part, covered by the authority attestation.

freshness.description: A consumer relies on this response until the earlier of `as_of` + `max_age_seconds` and `next_change_at`.

next_change_at.description: The next instant after `as_of` at which a term state changes on its own, if any.

term_states.description: One entry per term id of the versions that have taken effect by `as_of`, derived at `as_of` from `agreements` and `events`. A verifier that recomputes them and finds a difference rejects the response.

events.description: Append-only history, oldest first. The first event is `issued`; each later one carries the digest of the one before.

effectiveScope.description: A scope after narrowing. Lists may be empty, which permits nothing.

since.description: When the current status began. `withdrawn` and `ended` are final.

version.description: The version whose text applies: the version in force, or the last version that contained the term. For a withdrawn or ended term, as at `since`.

effective.description: For grants: the grant after every narrowing. For a withdrawn or ended grant, as at `since`.

narrowing.description: Operations that can only narrow a grant. They are cumulative and outlive later versions. Widening needs a new version or a new term.

recorded_at.description: When the authority appended the event.

received_at.description: For instructions from a party: when the authority received them. A narrowing, suspension or withdrawal from a party takes effect at this instant, or later only when `actor_signature` covers the later `effective_at`.

effective_at.description: When the event takes effect. Not before `recorded_at`, except for payment events and for a narrowing, suspension or withdrawal from a party (see `received_at`).

actor.description: Who caused the event: a `party_id`, or an authority `id`.

on_behalf_of.description: When an authorized representative acts: the participant's `party_id`.

channel.description: How the authority received the instruction.

version.description: For `issued` and `version_added`: the version that takes effect.

ref_seq.description: For `resumed`: the `suspended` event lifted. For `correction`: the event corrected.

ref_digest.description: For `issued` and `version_added`: the digest of the whole `agreements` item (`agreement`, `agreement_digest` and `signatures`), so the event chain fixes the signatures too. For `payment_recorded` and `asset_bound`: the digest of the payment or binding object.

keys_uri.description: For `authority_transferred`: the JWK Set of the transferring authority, on its origin, listing the key of `actor_signature`.

evidence.description: Digests of what was received, for example the withdrawal e-mail.

actor_signature.description: Signature by the actor. For `authority_transferred` it is required and covers the whole event without this member, and with it the history before the event. Otherwise it is optional and covers the instruction members.

prev_digest.description: base64url(SHA-256(UTF-8(JCS(previous event)))). null for the first event.

payment.description: Evidence that a payment was made. It never changes once recorded; its status follows from the payment events. The authority does not move money.

compensation_id.description: The compensation item paid, as it stands at `paid_at` (R15). Its payer and payee are the parties of every event about this payment.

reference.description: Invoice number, transfer reference or transaction id. Never an account or card number.

assetBinding.description: Registers one C2PA manifest as made under the listed grants. It never changes once recorded; `asset_unbound` ends it.

registered_by.description: The licensee that registered the asset.

media_type.description: The kind of asset, checked against the media types of the named grants.

mime_type.description: The asset's media type (RFC 6838), for example `image/jpeg`.

manifest_label.description: Label of the C2PA manifest that carries the `cawg.consent` reference to this record.

claim_signer.description: The certificate that signed the claim.

serial_number.description: Serial number of the signing certificate, in decimal.

certificate_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the DER-encoded signing certificate.

hard_binding.description: The claim's hashed URI reference to its hard-binding assertion.

alg.description: The algorithm in effect for the reference, written out even when the claim leaves it implicit.

hash.description: The hash bytes, base64url without padding.

asset_digest.description: SHA-256 of the exact file bytes as registered.
